name: Shared layers stay closed to specifics
when: Changes to integration layers, connectors, coordinators, dispatchers, registries, base classes and shared interfaces. Also driver modules that build or consume another module's descriptors, plans or specs.
expect: Move each specific behavior and its docs into its own module behind one generic extension point: a dispatcher created once at init and called once per hook, self-registration or package discovery selected by key, or the existing device/platform backend interface. Move construction and derivation of a structure into its owning module, which exposes a minimal API (one build and one consume entry point) and keeps internals private. Move non-inherent capabilities off base types into an opt-in protocol or mixin that callers depend on. The author confirms that adding a new variant or field touches no existing shared or driver file. Check: List the existing files that would have to change if (a) a second feature, implementation or vendor of this kind were added or removed next month, or (b) a new field or parameter were added to the structure this code builds or consumes. If the list includes the shared or driver module, flag it. Also flag shared or driver code that imports, names, looks up, branches on, special-cases, documents or builds the internals of a specific variant or of another module's structure. For any capability placed on a base type, ask whether it is inherent to what that base type represents, or only needed by today's subclasses.
why: Generic, shared or orchestrating code must not know about specific features, implementations, vendors, or the internals of structures owned by another module. Variants and new fields can then be added, removed or plugged in without editing it.

name: Bounded worst case on contended resources
when: GPU-side temporaries whose size scales with request or data length. Handlers or work placed on single-threaded or shared execution lanes, including liveness and health paths.
expect: Report the worst-case footprint. If it is unbounded or large, chunk the work with a fixed byte cap that preserves the unchunked version's ordering guarantees across chunk boundaries, and add a test that chunked output equals unchunked output. Move potentially blocking work off the single shared thread. Keep liveness probes off any lane that can block. Check: State the peak extra device memory, or the longest time it can hold the thread, for the longest realistic request or the slowest dependency (I/O, locks, registration, waiting on another component). Name the other work that shares that resource and would fail or stall meanwhile. If the cost cannot be stated, or grows without a cap, flag it.
why: Work that runs on a resource that other work shares and that may already be saturated, such as nearly full device memory or a single dispatcher thread, must have a bounded worst-case footprint. Otherwise it can OOM or stall everything else.
examples: team-v1-001: a GPU-side operation that can run while device memory or the KV pool is nearly full allocates temporaries whose size scales with the request or data size

name: Boundary contracts hold for every counterpart
when: Calling new APIs on components that have fallbacks. Reconnection and recovery paths. GPU event creation for transfers. LMCache-side workarounds for engine behavior.
why: Code that interacts across a process, version or project boundary must state the counterpart's contract explicitly. That contract must hold for every counterpart and context the code can meet at runtime, not just the common one.
examples: team-v1-003: a change alters LMCache behavior to compensate for how an upstream engine reports or handles state
team-v1-005: a reconnection or recovery path restores a connection to a peer that negotiated parameters during the initial handshake

when: Adding experimental or optional features (e.g. paged-Q ring capture) to lifecycle hooks in lmcache/integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector.py (__init__, register_kv_caches, save_kv_layer, wait_for_save)
expect: The MP connector is the shared vLLM integration layer for all features. Experimental engine-side features are reached through a dispatcher created once in __init__ (from lmcache.experimental.engine_side import init_dispatcher; self.dispatcher = init_dispatcher(kwargs)). Each hook forwards with self.dispatcher.dispatch("<hook>", **kwargs). Feature-named attributes such as self.q_ring_capture, and `is not None` branches on them, are violations. save_kv_layer is a no-op on the core MP path, so feature-specific docs belong in the feature's module, not in the connector docstring. (apply P1)
examples: vLLM connector added `self.<feature>` plus `if self.<feature> is not None:` blocks in `register_kv_caches`/`wait_for_save`. Reviewer asked for `self.dispatcher = init_dispatcher(kwargs)` from `lmcache.experimental.engine_side` in `__init__` and `self.dispatcher.dispatch("register_kv_caches", **kwargs)` in the hook.

MP connector's no-op `save_kv_layer` was filled with an experimental feature's logic and docstring. Reviewer asked for `self.dispatcher.dispatch("save_kv_layer", **kwargs)` with the behavior documented in the experimental module.

`if device_type == "musa"` branches in multiprocess/transfer code for event record, stream wait and IPC handle export. These should go through a device backend method that MUSA and CUDA each implement.
A generic transfer path imports or calls vendor-specific stream/event APIs directly, or adds a vendor-only fallback, instead of going through a per-device backend implementation.

The MP coordinator's shared HTTP API layer called `ctx.controllers.get(FleetEvictionController)` to serve that controller's endpoints. Controllers can be out-of-tree, so the reviewer asked that each controller package register its own HTTP routes instead of the shared layer hardcoding which controllers exist.

All spec implementations lived in one large file with manual registration, causing growth and merge conflicts. Reviewer asked for one file per spec in a package, loaded by dynamic scanning, so a new spec changes no existing line.
An `if/elif` chain on engine type selected the format detection logic. Reviewer asked for a strategy pattern: a set of per-engine format detector objects selected by key.

when: Changes to lmcache/v1/multiprocess/modules/lmcache_driven_transfer.py and its use of transfer_descriptor and the transfer plan (kernel/object groups, layout desc, sliding-window block-id cutting)
expect: lmcache_driven_transfer.py is the driver and must stay very thin. The transfer descriptor and transfer plan modules own their structures, and each should expose one build function and one consume function, hiding internal functions and structures as much as possible. Helpers such as get_layout_desc (which also needs a signature change), block-id cutting and build_object_group_transfer_descriptor_from_cache_context belong in the descriptor/plan modules. A new kernel-group or object-group parameter should change only those modules and leave lmcache_driven_transfer.py untouched. (apply P1)
examples: lmcache_driven_transfer.py defined public functions that derived layout metadata from the cache context and built per-kernel-group and per-object-group transfer descriptors. The reviewer asked to move them into the descriptor/plan module behind one build function and one consume function each, so that a new kernel-group or object-group parameter would not require edits to the driver.

The top-level 'cache context -> resolved transfer descriptor' builder was moved into the descriptor module. To avoid an import cycle, that module uses duck typing and imports the cache-context class only under TYPE_CHECKING.

when: Adding methods or hooks to the View base class in lmcache/v1/mp_coordinator/views/base.py, or to similar coordinator base types
expect: Durability (get_durable_components / DurableComponent) is not inherent to a coordinator View. A view rebuilt from the event stream alone needs nothing durable, and components outside the View hierarchy may also need durability. It belongs in an opt-in durability protocol that callers depend on, not as a default method on View, even if all current views happen to implement it. (apply P1)
examples: `get_durable_components` was added as a method of `View` only because all existing Views implement it; the reviewer asked whether every future View will have it and whether a non-View class never will, pointing toward a separate interface/mixin.

tests.note: base holds a field only some subclasses use; AI suggested the opposite (hoist caching into base)

when: Code that receives the engine's GPU kv_caches: KVFormatSpec in lmcache/v1/gpu_connector/kv_format/specs/base.py, and any spec, helper, adapter, cache, registry or closure
expect: Engine KV cache tensors, and views or containers of them, may be retained only by the single owner whose state is cleared on engine disconnect. A spec or helper that stores kv_caches (e.g. self.kv_caches in KVFormatSpec.__init__) pins GPU memory after disconnect, which is a memory leak. Specs should carry only class-level layout metadata and take kv_caches per call, or the diff must show where teardown releases the reference. (apply P2)
examples: A KVFormatSpec object stored the raw `kv_caches` list as an attribute. The reviewer flagged the memory-leak risk and asked that all references to the GPU KV tensors be removable when the serving engine disconnects.

when: In-place writes into vLLM paged KV blocks, e.g. apply_kv_compaction_moves in lmcache/integration/vllm/experimental/kv_compaction.py and its worker wiring
expect: vLLM owns the paged KV blocks, and prefix caching can share one physical block across requests. Writing into a shared destination block changes another request's KV. The writing function must document exclusive block ownership as a precondition, and the worker wiring must guarantee private blocks through copy-on-write or by excluding those requests from prefix caching. (apply P2)
examples: a function that compacts or relocates KV inside vLLM paged blocks without checking whether a block is shared via the prefix cache

when: Adding or modifying MP engine submodules (transfer modules, ManagementModule/ping, BlendV3Module, liveness reaping), or design docs under docs/design/v1/multiprocess/
expect: The MP engine is an ownership tree. The engine context owns the storage manager and every submodule, and each submodule holds only a context reference. Cross-submodule needs, such as liveness touching transfer contexts (InstanceLivenessTarget) or reaping notifying BlendV3Module (InstanceReapListener), must go through context methods that dispatch to the owner. Constructor injection into ManagementModule, setters and stored sibling references are not allowed. Design docs must describe the same structure. (apply P2)
examples: ManagementModule (answers PING) needed to touch or reap instances tracked by the GPU/CPU transfer modules. The reviewer asked it to call `self._ctx.<method>` and let MPEngineContext dispatch, instead of receiving the transfer modules by injection.
BlendV3Module and the GPU/CPU transfer modules are siblings under MPEngineContext, so none of them should hold a reference to another.

when: Propagating per-instance state such as storage capacity from lmcache/v1/distributed/storage_manager.py to the MP coordinator (http_apis/events_api.py, server_config registry)
expect: The cache-event pipeline from instances to the coordinator is the existing propagation channel. Capacity should be a new cache-event type (e.g. "config"), and the server_config registry should become a consumer of cache events. The events_api handler should only forward events, without unpacking capacity_reports or calling server_config.update inline. The parallel CapacitySnapshot/revision snapshot path is a second mechanism and should be removed. (apply P2)
examples: Instance capacity was sent to the coordinator both as cache events and via a snapshot API; reviewer asked for a new 'config' cache event type consumed by the server config registry instead
An HTTP handler unpacked the reported capacity payload and updated the registry directly rather than forwarding it as an event

when: GPU gather/scatter ops on the KV cache, e.g. apply_kv_compaction_moves in lmcache/integration/vllm/experimental/kv_compaction.py (kv_cache[dst] = kv_cache[src])
expect: KV compaction is likely to run when the KV pool is nearly full. Advanced indexing kv_cache[src] materializes a temporary proportional to the number of moved slots, which can OOM. Process the moves in chunks with a fixed byte cap. Preserve the single gather's read-before-write semantics across chunk boundaries, because a destination slot may be a later move's source. Add a test that the chunked result equals the unchunked one. (apply P3)
examples: KV compaction or block-move gather allocating a buffer sized to a 128K-token request; chunk under a byte cap and ensure earlier destinations never overwrite later sources
a gather kernel that materializes all selected blocks at once instead of in capped batches

when: Adding request handlers or changing their dispatch mode in the multiprocess server, especially PING/liveness and REGISTER_KV_CACHE
expect: All SYNC handlers run on one server-side dispatcher thread. REGISTER_KV_CACHE is already SYNC and can block that thread for a while, so PING/liveness on SYNC would time out spuriously. Liveness belongs on BLOCKING dispatch in the shared worker pool, so that a timeout reflects real pool saturation, or on a dedicated responder thread. New SYNC handlers must be shown to be short and non-blocking. (apply P3)
examples: A PR moved PING to SYNC dispatch while REGISTER_KV_CACHE was also SYNC and can occupy the dispatcher thread for a while. The reviewer asked to put PING on BLOCKING with the normal thread pool for now.
Long-term plan from the same review: move REGISTER_KV_CACHE to BLOCKING dispatch and give PING its own responder thread.

when: LMCache-side changes in the vLLM connector that react to vLLM's reporting, e.g. requests appearing in finished_sending / finished_recving
expect: Maintainers expect vLLM to report only requests that performed a store operation in finished_sending, so a load-only request showing up there is a deviation from the expected semantics. The PR must explain that semantics and the observed deviation, and justify why LMCache rather than vLLM is the right place for the fix, or link the upstream issue or PR. (apply P4)
examples: filtering load-only requests out of vLLM's finished_sending, where only requests that performed a store should appear

when: Reconnect/recovery callbacks in lmcache/integration/vllm/vllm_multi_process_adapter.py after the LMCache server restarts while vLLM stays alive
expect: Chunk size is negotiated at handshake. A restarted LMCache server reverts to its configured value (e.g. 256), while the vLLM scheduler and worker adapters keep the negotiated value (e.g. 640). Recovery must re-negotiate the chunk size and verify it against the adapters' cached value before re-registering KV and marking the connection healthy. A mismatch must be handled explicitly, not ignored. (apply P4)
examples: vLLM multiprocess adapter reconnecting to a restarted LMCache server that only re-registers KV and never renegotiates chunk size

when: Creating or recording GPU events for KV transfers in the MP adapter/connector (create_event / create_and_record_event), or merging event creation across load and store paths
expect: LMCache-driven transfers cross the process boundary and need interprocess (IPC) events. Engine-driven transfers need normal local events. Async engine-driven transfers must still create and keep a local event and must never pass None. A single context-agnostic event-creation path is wrong: the event type must be selected explicitly for each transfer context. (apply P4)
examples: The reviewer asked that event creation select the type from the actual transfer context. LMCache-driven transfers get an IPC event, and engine-driven transfers get a normal local event. Async engine-driven transfers keep a local event rather than passing None.

when: lmcache/integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector.py and its version variants (e.g. 0180, 0201) calling new methods on the worker adapter
expect: The connector can fall back to vLLM's vendored LMCacheMPWorkerAdapter. That adapter lacks newer LMCache-owned APIs such as create_and_record_event, so under fallback the call raises AttributeError at request time. Before the change, the connector created the event itself (torch_dev.Event(interprocess=True)). Each new adapter call needs a feature-detecting compatibility helper, removal of the fallback, or a sync of the vendored API. The fix applies to both the load and store paths and to every version-specific connector variant. (apply P4)
examples: A connector still fell back to vLLM's vendored LMCacheMPWorkerAdapter. The PR moved event creation, which the connector used to do inline, into a new `create_and_record_event` method that exists only on the LMCache-owned adapter. The fix had to cover both the load and store paths and every version-specific connector variant.

when: a docstring explains in prose a multi-step or non-obvious state transformation that the reader has to simulate in their head
expect: Ask for a self-contained worked example in the docstring that shows the initial state, the arguments of successive calls, and the resulting state after each call.
why: Prose alone for stateful transformations is ambiguous and hard to verify, while a concrete trace makes both intent and bugs visible.
examples: a function tracking block ids under speculative relocation, documented only in prose
concern: Docstrings for non-obvious state changes need a worked example

when: a change adds, refactors or touches code that is used only by the legacy non-MP (non-multiprocess) mode, or adds or modifies a base class or interface whose methods are split between MP-mode use and non-MP-only use
expect: Ask the author to mark non-MP-only code paths with the project's deprecation annotation so they emit a deprecation warning. For base classes and interfaces, ask them to document per method whether MP mode requires it or only legacy non-MP mode uses it. Legacy-only code must not be left silently maintained without a marker.
why: Non-MP mode is legacy and slated for removal. Its code must be identifiable so that implementers know what is actually required and later cleanups know what to delete.
examples: A function used only by non-MP mode was refactored without any warning. The reviewer asked for the `lmcache_deprecate` annotation on it.
A base class defined many methods with no indication of which ones MP mode uses. The reviewer asked the author to clarify which are used in MP mode and which are used only in non-MP mode.
concern: Explicitly mark legacy non-MP-only code (deprecation annotation or documentation) so it is identifiable for removal
